subject: ClearLend — Post-discovery and dedicated-sizing kickoff
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emma Park <emma@clearlend.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: ClearLend — Post-discovery and dedicated-sizing kickoff

Hi Emma — great conversation earlier today. Thanks for walking through the ClearLend payment flows and the latency-sensitive portions of your reconciliation pipeline. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the dedicated-sizing call: 

Recap (30s):
- Primary use case: near‑real‑time statement reconciliation and fraud signal enrichment for 1. user-facing transactions, 2. end-of-day batch reconciliation.
- Key constraints: peak bursts during settlement windows (estimated today to be ~1k–2k req/min), hard 95th‑pct latency SLO of 200ms for the enrichment path, and end‑of‑day throughput for batch scoring.

Request for the sizing call:
- We recommend a 60–75 minute technical kickoff (Dedicated sizing + demo + ops checklist). Karthik (cc'd) will lead the deep dive on throughput and latency tuning.
- To make the session productive, could you share rough numbers ahead of time? Prefer CSV or bullet list: peak qps/reqs per second, average tokens per request (if applicable), % of requests that require context/windowing, and expected concurrency during peak windows.

Proposed time slots (all in ET for convenience):
- Wed Mar 17, 10:00–11:15 ET
- Wed Mar 17, 14:00–15:15 ET
- Thu Mar 18, 09:00–10:15 ET

Attachments: dedicated_sizing_checklist.pdf (PDF, 52KB) — short intake checklist and a template for traffic profile.

Agenda (high level): intro + discovery recap (10m) -> throughput profile and sample traffic (15m) -> model/config options & quantization/latency levers (20m) -> scheduling/pool sizing and next steps (15–30m).

If any of the slots work, I’ll lock the calendar and send an invite with a short preread. If procurement needs to be looped, please add them on reply. Thanks — looking forward to the next step.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147

Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0400

Thanks, Soojin — that recap looks right. We'd like to take the first slot: Wed Mar 17, 10:00–11:15 ET. I'll add Jake (procurement) on this thread.

Quick note on numbers: I'll send a short CSV by EOD with observed peak qps and a sample of the enrichment payloads. For context: our peak customer-facing bursts happen 09:30–10:30 ET and 20:00–21:00 ET; daily batch runs at 02:00 ET.

Agenda request: please confirm a short agenda we can distribute internally so procurement knows the meeting goals.

—Emma

Emma — confirmed for Wed Mar 17, 10:00–11:15 ET. I've reserved the slot here: https://cal.redwood.com/slot/3k9f-9a2 and will send a calendar invite in a minute.

Updated agenda (to share with procurement):
1) Introductions & goals (5m)
2) Engineering discovery — traffic profile & sample requests (15m)
3) Throughput/latency sizing exercise (live Q&A) — expected concurrency, burst handling, and SLO mapping (25m)
4) Operational controls & options (dedicated pool, burst policies, KV/prefix caching) (10m)
5) Next steps: timeline, mutual action items, procurement checklist (10m)

Pre-reads attached: sample_traffic_template.csv (small template to paste a traffic sample) and the short Dedicated sizing checklist. If you can drop the CSV into the thread before the call that’d be ideal — Karthik and I will prioritize the tuning exercise around the sample.

Thanks — Karthik, can you confirm you'll join as SE and bring an initial sizing sketch?

Cheers,
Soojin

Attachments: sample_traffic_template.csv (CSV, 4KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Park <emma@clearlend.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearLend — Post-discovery and dedicated-sizing kickoff

Emma — I'll be on the call and will prepare an initial sizing sketch based on the CSV. I plan to cover: baseline GPU footprint scenarios, batching/latency tradeoffs, and quick recommendations on cache windows that tend to cut token costs without sacrificing 95th‑pct latency.

If you have any sample payloads (anonymized) or a rough distribution of tokens per request, please drop them in the thread — that materially changes the sizing. Looking forward to Wednesday at 10am ET.
